findings.suggested_fix: In MATCHING/linked_groups_socio.do:27, load `congruent` instead of `target` (`use linked_before linked_after age congruent legibility `vars' using `"`temp'"', clear`), then after line 35 add `assert inlist(congruent,0,1)` and `gen byte target = 1 - congruent` (and optionally assert `quietly sum target` / `assert abs(100*r(mean) - 28.2473163170171) < 1e-9` against `\pctTargetOfTable` in MATCHING/results/create_figures_SSHA2025_tgt.tex:22).
findings.title: temp_tgt.dta does not contain variable target, causing use at line 27 to abort with r(111)
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 27 runs `use linked_before linked_after age target legibility `vars' using `"`temp'"', clear` where `temp` is `temp_tgt.dta`. However, `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do` generates `congruent=namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast` at line 73, saves `temp_tgt.dta` at line 119, reloads `temp_tgt.dta` at line 130, and only generates `target=!(namefrst==fs_namefrst & namelast==fs_namelast)` in memory at line 138 without ever re-saving `temp_tgt.dta`.
findings.why_it_matters: Running `MATCHING/linked_groups_socio.do` will immediately fail at line 27 with Stata error `variable target not found` (`r(111)`), producing no output file `MATCHING/results/linked_groups_socio.md`.

findings.how_to_check: Check CODE/usa00647_for_SSHA2025_socio_demo_char.do:3764-3768 and MATCHING/_figs_tgt_run.log:1052-1053,1138: `recode incnonwg (1 9=.)` makes 37,609,917 changes and leaves only `incnonwg==2` (13,426,942 records; 37,609,917 + 13,426,942 = 51,036,859) as non-missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Change MATCHING/linked_groups_socio.do:52 from `recode incnonwg (1 9=.)` to `recode incnonwg (0 9=.)` so that `incnonwg==1` ("Less than $50 nonwage, nonsalary income") remains in the non-missing denominator `d1..d4`. Then either add a label for `v1=="incnonwg" & v2==1` (e.g., `"Nonwage inc.<50"`) or `drop if v1=="incnonwg" & v2==1` after `postclose` at line 88 if only the `Nonwage inc.>50` row is desired.
findings.title: Recoding incnonwg==1 to missing leaves incnonwg==2 as the only non-missing value, forcing its within-group share to 100.0% in every column
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 52 copies `recode incnonwg (1 9=.)` from `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:351`, and lines 76-85 compute each category's share within link-status group `g` as `100 * count(grp==g & incnonwg==val) / count(grp==g & !missing(incnonwg))`. In IPUMS 1940 (`CODE/usa00647_for_SSHA2025_socio_demo_char.do:3764-3768`), `incnonwg` is coded `0` (N/A), `1` (<$50), `2` ($50+), and `9` (Missing). In Figure 4 of `create_figures_SSHA2025.do`, recoding `1` to `.` worked because that script computed linkage rates *within* each category (`sum linked_before if incnonwg==2`). Here, recoding `1` to `.` leaves `2` as the only non-missing value of `incnonwg` in `temp_tgt.dta` (`MATCHING/_figs_tgt_run.log:1052-1053,1138`), so the numerator (`grp==g & incnonwg==2`) equals the denominator (`grp==g & !missing(incnonwg)`) for every group `g=1..4`.
findings.why_it_matters: The `Nonwage inc.>50` row in `MATCHING/results/linked_groups_socio.md` will report `100.0 | 100.0 | 100.0 | 100.0` across all four link-status groups (`Both`, `After only`, `Neither`, `Before only`) instead of the true share of each group with nonwage income over $50 (~26-28%).

structured_output.summary: The review covers the new script MATCHING/linked_groups_socio.do and its brief review/briefs/2026-11-19-linked-groups-socio.md. Two verified blockers in MATCHING/linked_groups_socio.do prevent the script from running and from computing valid shares for nonwage income: first, line 27 attempts to load variable `target` from `temp_tgt.dta`, but `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do` saves `temp_tgt.dta` at line 119 with `congruent` before generating `target` at line 138 (`r(111)`); second, line 52 executes `recode incnonwg (1 9=.)`, which recodes the `<$50` category (`1`) to missing `.` and leaves `incnonwg==2` (`Nonwage inc.>50`) as the sole non-missing value, causing its within-group share among non-missing records to evaluate to 100.0% in all four link-status groups. All other 14 socio-demographic recodes, group partitioning, scalar survival across dataset replacement, and verification assertions against create_figures_SSHA2025_tgt.tex were verified clean.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
